mechanism_interpretation.primary_evidence: The book first contacts caddy collision geometry at8.500s while grip still commands near-closed. Thereafter relative pose rotates/drifts. At11.6s the new H40 chunk simultaneously widens the gripper target and changes the EEF reference; recorded clamping forces become much smaller before final bilateral loss at12.054s. This supports coupled approach/constraint/grip coordination failure; unique causation is not established without an independently designed intervention.
mechanism_interpretation.no_full_open_release: Every installed gripper target in11.6–12.054s remains below the corresponding pre-command actual aperture; this is not a commanded full-open release. Increasing target opening can reduce closing position error and holding force even while the target is still narrower than the actual fingers.
mechanism_interpretation.native_grasp_label: Original native_grasp has227 short true intervals and never remains true for the Teacher0.3s verification dwell. Bilateral pad contact lasts much longer. Centroid-velocity difference is evaluated at different points and includes a rigid-rotation lever-arm term; individual false native_grasp samples are not proof of physical release. The original predicate is retained, not repaired or rescored.
mechanism_interpretation.tracking: Command_i precedes interval_i; TCP tracking is measured at the actual next observation, not against the pre-command state. Saved forces at an observation reflect the preceding command. Chunk jumps and contact constraints coexist; tracking error alone is not a unique cause.
mechanism_interpretation.teacher_lift: The largest actual native book rise is54.809mm, below the Teacher60mm lift-transition condition. That is a Teacher-stage comparison, not an added student task-success criterion.
mechanism_interpretation.counterfactual: No new physics, friction/force change, WBC tuning, action repair or new model query. This is a temporal mechanism analysis, not a new causal experiment or successful demonstration.
